Hello, Ricardo! It's Elena, from the guesthouse in Dubrovnik. You asked me about next year, so here is my advice. If you come in August again, you will see the city at its busiest. There will be cruise ships near the harbor and long lines at the city walls. But if you come in May or in October, you will find a different city. The streets will be peaceful, the sea will still be warm, and you will have the old town almost for yourself. And one more thing. If you stay inside the walls, you will meet the families who still live here. There are not many of us now. If you tell me your dates soon, I will keep your old room for you.

My family has lived inside these walls for four generations. When I was a boy, about five thousand people lived in the old town. Now there are fewer than two thousand. My neighbors moved out, one by one, because the rent was too high. If this continues, my children won't live here. But please understand, I am not against tourists. They are good for the city, and my little cafe needs them. The new rules help a lot: fewer cruise ships, and more visitors in spring and autumn. If the city protects the old town, and the visitors respect it, we will all win. If not, in twenty years there will be nobody here to sell you a coffee.

First Ricardo and Elena walked into the old town at ten in the morning. Then they saw three cruise ships near the harbor. After that the main street was so overcrowded that they could not walk. Then Elena said that her neighbors moved out because the rent was too high. Next they climbed to a quiet street behind the walls. In the end Ricardo said: If I come back in May, I will stay here.
